topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture series, outlines student learning objectives, and frames the clinical and biological scope of cancer biology.

topics.label: Biological concepts and experimental models of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: They define cancer as a failure of differentiation and tissue architecture driven by genetic and epigenetic alterations, while evaluating the strengths and limits of in vitro models used to study it.

topics.label: Invasion, metastasis, and progression from benign to malignant tumors
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the morphological and histological features that distinguish benign from malignant tumors, the routes of metastatic dissemination, and the stepwise progression of precursor lesions.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature conventions and exceptions
topics.groupedBecause: It outlines the standardized rules and exceptions for naming benign and malignant neoplasms based on their tissue and cellular origins.

topics.label: Pathophysiological causes of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: It details the local mechanical, tissue-destructive, and systemic physiological mechanisms through which tumors cause clinical illness and death.

topics.label: Comparative tumor incidence across humans and other species
topics.groupedBecause: They examine patterns of cancer incidence and tissue susceptibility across human populations and diverse multicellular organisms.

topics.label: Principles and clinical methods of cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: They address the rationale, histological basis, and practical limitations of population-level cancer screening and early detection across different organ sites.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the session by reviewing the learning outcomes and providing housekeeping notes for upcoming practicals and lectures.
